prompt: Please review PR 361 in pr/361/changes.diff and description.md before we merge it. It adds a generic event receiver and customer notification path to Relay Gateway. This is the security sign-off before a wider tenant rollout: the service accepts externally generated events and can affect customer systems, so I need concrete consequences in this deployment rather than style commentary. Read the changed code with the relevant contracts, configuration, and callers, and separate real release blockers from harmless-looking values or existing conventions. Write the review to REVIEW.md at the top of the project. End REVIEW.md with a fenced json list of findings, with each object containing location (path/to/file.ext:LINE, using line numbers from the project files as they are now), severity (critical, high, medium, low or nit), issue, and fix.

rubric.criterion: Each important finding explains the concrete consequence in this service and gives a fix a developer can act on, without inventing problems (code cannot check this because it cannot judge whether the explanation is concrete or the fix is actionable).

findingsKey.finding: The receiver verifies a JSON re-serialization rather than the exact request bytes, so valid provider signatures can fail or an alternate representation can be accepted under a different digest.
The secret-derived signature is compared with ordinary string equality, which exposes a timing signal to an attacker probing the webhook endpoint.

A correctly signed delivery is accepted, stored, and notified without enforcing the documented timestamp window or deduplicating its delivery identifier, allowing replayed events to trigger customer actions again.
The callback posts to the customer-supplied URL and follows redirects without destination validation, allowing a tenant setting to reach internal services or cloud metadata.
Missing webhook configuration silently selects a shared hard-coded secret, so an unconfigured deployment can accept requests signed with a value known from the source.
The invalid-signature diagnostic includes the complete secret-bearing signature header, exposing reusable authentication material to log readers and retained log systems.
